item.title: OpenRouter Models Compared: 2026 Guide to Speed and Cost
item.guid: title:openrouter models compared 2026 guide to speed and cost
item.description: TL;DR OpenRouter aggregates hundreds of large language models across dozens of independent host providers through a unified OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Frontier reasoning models such as Claude 3. 7 Sonnet and GPT-4o lead in complex agentic planning, while DeepSeek V3. 2 and Qwen 2. 5 Coder deliver comparable coding outputs at roughly one-tenth the cost. Built-in meta-routers like openrouter/auto and :nitro variants optimize for market popularity and raw throughput, but introduce provider-dependent latency variations.

item.title: What Is Ingress? Inbound Traffic, Kubernetes, and Modern Gateways Explained
item.guid: title:what is ingress inbound traffic kubernetes and modern gateways explained
item.description: TL;DR Ingress defines any network traffic entering a private boundary or cluster from an external client or network. In traditional networking, ingress operates at Layers 3 and 4 to enforce firewall rules, mitigate spoofing via packet filtering, and manage network address translation. In cloud-native systems, Kubernetes Ingress and the Kubernetes Gateway API act at Layer 7 to route HTTP, HTTPS, and gRPC traffic to backend microservices. Application and AI infrastructure require protocol-aware ingress gateways to handle authentication, dynamic rate limiting, load balancing, and content filtering. For teams running model inference workloads, Bifrost , an open-source AI gateway by Maxim AI, manages incoming Layer 7 traffic to deliver failover, caching, and enterprise governance across diverse providers. In network engineering and distributed computing, ingress refers to any data traffic entering a network boundary from an external source.

item.title: Adaptive Stopping of Streamed Reasoning for Language Model Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610. 27981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reasoning-enabled language model agents can incur substantial computation before acting, although the reasoning needed varies across decisions. Existing stopping signals, such as confidence and intermediate-answer stability, can vary in effectiveness across reasoning models; signals obtained from hidden states or token probabilities also require internal access that may be unavailable or impractical. We introduce StreamStop, which learns model-specific stopping policies offline from prefix-level action agreement. A frozen prefix reader encodes available reasoning text for a lightweight stop head, allowing stopping without access to the reasoning model's internal signals. We construct and publicly release a dataset of agent reasoning trajectories with prefix-level action annotations.

item.title: I Tested Four Local AI Models on a Literary Translation. Gemma 4 Won — With a Catch.
item.guid: title:i tested four local ai models on a literary translation gemma 4 won with a catch
item.description: I Tested Four Local AI Models on a Literary Translation. Gemma 4 Won — With a Catch. Four local GGUF models, one English novel, 20 matched passages — and a lesson in speed, Serbian grammar, and translation failure. I wanted to answer a practical question: if I have a Windows laptop with an NVIDIA GTX 1650 Ti and 4 GB of VRAM, which small local language model should I actually trust to translate an English novel into Serbian? The obvious candidate was TranslateGemma, a model designed for translation. But after its first run, I tried a general-purpose Gemma 4 model, followed by Qwen3 and Qwen3.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: LazyDesk AI: Let AI Handle the Busywork
item.guid: title:lazydesk ai let ai handle the busywork
item.description: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built Demo Code How I Built It LazyDesk AI: Let AI Handle the Busywork This is my submission for the "Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady" ( https://dev. to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week3-2026-10-19 ). What I Built I built LazyDesk AI, an AI-powered productivity assistant designed to make everyday work a little easier. We all have tasks that consume time without requiring much creativity: reading lengthy documents, organizing notes, identifying important action items, and figuring out what needs to be done next. LazyDesk AI aims to simplify this process. Users can provide their documents and notes, and the application helps summarize information, extract important tasks, and turn scattered information into a more organized action plan.

item.title: AtomSD: Procedural Atom-Guided Self-Distillation for LLM Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610. 26926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) possess broad factual knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, but solving complex tasks also requires procedural knowledge about how to act. Existing approaches often represent procedural knowledge through trajectories or bundled skills, limiting flexible reuse across interaction histories. This paper introduces Procedural Atoms, fine-grained and independently applicable units that represent Intent, When, Do, and Avoid guidance. Building on this representation, we propose AtomSD, an Atom-guided Self-Distillation framework in which the learner continually extracts Procedural Atoms from its own successful trajectories and distills them into the evolving policy through Atom-conditioned supervision and task-reward optimization. Comprehensive experiments show that AtomSD consistently outperforms strong reward-based and distillation methods, exceeding the state-of-the-art baseline by up to 9.

item.title: RealControlBench: A Benchmark for Interpretability-Informed Fine-Grained Control of LLMs and Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610. 27295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing steering benchmarks are built around simplified, isolated generation tasks and evaluate a single behavioral attribute under controlled settings that do not reflect the diversity and complexity of practical deployment. As a result, performance on these benchmarks provides only a limited picture of how steering methods perform in the real world. We therefore introduce RealControlBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating fine-grained steering of LLMs and LLM agents across diverse behavioral targets and interaction settings. RealControlBench extends steering evaluation beyond isolated generations to complex, execution-grounded, multi-turn agent interactions, covering five complementary dimensions: instruction-following control, agentic tool-use decision control, reasoning-performance steering, reasoning-length control, and trajectory-conditioned safety awareness. Rather than measuring steering success alone, the benchmark jointly evaluates target controllability and capability preservation, including instruction following, reasoning performance, and downstream agent utility and safety.

item.title: DStill: Trajectory Consistency Distillation for Accelerated One-Step Drafting in Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
item.description: arXiv:2610. 27379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Block-diffusion speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by drafting multiple tokens in parallel. However, one-step drafting in discrete diffusion is limited by token factorization error: each token is predicted from the same masked block, without conditioning on the tokens selected at other positions in that step. This can produce inconsistent drafts and reduce acceptance length. Iterative refinement mitigates this limitation by conditioning later predictions on previously committed tokens, though additional passes increase drafting cost. To address this trade-off between draft fidelity and inference latency, we introduce DStill, a two-stage framework that distills a target-conditioned drafter's own multi-step refinement into one-step drafting.

item.title: TeCoP: Accelerating Diffusion Large Language Model Decoding via Tentative Context Pipelining
item.description: arXiv:2610. 27583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) predict multiple token positions per forward pass, yet block-wise decoders serialize generation and repeatedly recompute stable predictions. We attribute this inefficiency to coupling a prediction's readiness for irreversible commitment with its utility as context. We introduce Tentative Context Pipelining (TeCoP), a training-free decoder that decouples these roles through staggered block-parallel pipelining and draft-and-verify. TeCoP reuses stable but uncommitted predictions as provisional cross-block context, with commitment governed by confidence and stability checks. Across four LLaDA and Dream dLLMs on GSM8K, Minerva MATH, and MBPP, TeCoP reduces number of forward evaluations by up to 87% and achieves up to 7.

item.title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
item.description: arXiv:2610. 28457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: General-purpose multimodal models have shown promise as direct robot action policies, yet whether they grasp the physics underlying real-world interactions and can apply that understanding to guide action remains underexplored. We investigate this question using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed, examining tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability. Contact-rich manipulation requires interpreting tactile feedback and adjusting actions after obstruction. Existing learned tactile policies acquire these capabilities through specialized pretraining and per-task optimization, with substantial data and training costs. We present GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action.

item.title: Rethinking How to Remember: Beyond Atomic Facts in Lifelong LLM Agent Memory
item.description: arXiv:2605. 19952v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To enable reliable long-term interaction, LLM agents require a memory system that can faithfully store, efficiently retrieve, and deeply reason over accumulated dialogue history. Most existing methods adopt an extracted fact based paradigm: handcrafted static prompts compress raw dialogues into atomic facts, which are then stored, matched, and injected into downstream reasoning. Nevertheless, such fact-centric designs inevitably discard fine-grained details in original dialogues and fail to support deep reasoning over scattered isolated facts. Moreover, static prompts cannot maintain consistent extraction granularity across diverse dialogue styles. To address these limitations, we propose TriMem, which maintains three coexisting representation granularities, including raw dialogue segments anchored by source identifiers for storage fidelity, extracted atomic facts for efficient memory retrieval, synthesized profiles that aggregate dispersed facts into holistic semantic understanding for deep reasoning.

item.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
item.description: arXiv:2610. 23234v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. An LLM judge can score the performance of the subagents, but these scores depend on the judge's own assessment of the quality of subagents' responses. We present MultiAgent-OPD, which combines on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning to jointly train a shared-parameter Leader-Searcher-Answerer team end to end. We first train a Teacher in a Searcher-Answerer workflow using answer correctness.

item.title: A Theoretical Analysis of Environment-Aware Out-of-Distribution Detection for Vision-Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2610. 27211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continual vision-language models (VLMs) encounter a stream of environments and must also reject inputs that do not belong to the environment at hand. Class information from earlier environments can aid out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, yet existing detectors score each environment in isolation, and when previous environments help or hurt is theoretically unclear. We develop a theory of environment-aware OOD detection built on contribution scores, pairwise cosine expectations measuring how the image and text features of one environment align with those of another. We propose a cross-environment maximum-concept-matching (MCM) score with two terms: a primary term matching the test image against the current class texts, and a secondary term matching it against the class texts of a previous environment, weighted by the intra-modal alignment between the two environments. We prove that, under a positive environment transition and a bounded class-matching margin for OOD inputs, this score attains a false-positive rate no larger than that of the standard MCM detector at an adjusted threshold.

item.title: Elicitation or Expansion? Demystifying Gains from Agent Harness Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610. 27889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent studies in harness optimization have shown substantial performance gains in language model agents without updating model weights. A well-designed harness more effectively leverages the underlying model's capabilities by shaping context, tool use, and execution workflows. However, na\"ive success rates alone do not fully characterize whether optimized harness yields more reliable success on tasks already within reach (elicitation) or a broader range of solvable tasks (expansion). This distinction is crucial for recursive self-improvement and evolutionary search, as expansion may provide a broader range of successful experiences to push the capability boundaries. Despite the growing significance, this distinction remains underexplored in harness optimization.

item.title: RANGER: Retrieval Agent for Navigating Graphs with Semantic Evaluation Rewards
item.description: arXiv:2610. 28010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models and Reinforcement Learning offers a promising direction for complex sequential decision-making tasks, such as multi-hop question answering over knowledge graphs. While LLMs provide strong semantic understanding and reasoning capabilities, they often struggle with precise, multi-step navigation in structured environments. Conversely, RL agents excel at learning navigation policies but are hindered by the difficulty of designing semantically meaningful reward functions. This paper introduces a novel hybrid approach in which an LLM serves as a mentor to an RL agent during training by providing dense, semantically informed reward signals. The RL agent, built on a Transformer-based policy and trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization, learns to navigate a knowledge graph to retrieve relevant information.

item.title: Self-Credit: Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Agentic RL via Intra-group Rescaling
item.description: arXiv:2610. 28388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are commonly trained with RLVR, but the sparse nature of typical RLVR rewards makes credit assignment challenging, especially for long-horizon tasks. We propose Self-Credit, an end-to-end agentic RL method that creates dense supervision signals from sparse outcome rewards using self-generated credit assignment via intra-group rescaling. Self-Credit builds on group-based RL with three components. First, during its rollouts, the policy model generates summaries with citations to earlier turns containing critical evidence, which serve as self-generated credit. Second, we refine this model-generated credit with intra-group rescaling, which compares cited actions across successful and failed rollouts for the same prompt.

item.title: Introducing PerceptionBench
item.guid: title:introducing perceptionbench
item.description: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models Authors Kimi Team We are releasing PerceptionBench , a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities— discovered from how today's models fail, not defined in advance. From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.

item.title: Kimi K2.5: Visual Agentic Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k2 5 visual agentic intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K2. 5, the most powerful open-source model to date. Kimi K2. 5 builds on Kimi K2 with continued pretraining over approximately 15T mixed visual and text tokens. Built as a native multimodal model, K2. 5 delivers state-of-the-art coding and vision capabilities and a self-directed agent swarm paradigm.
